draft.title: Circadian rhythm sleep disorders
card: The circadian rhythm is the body's daily cycle of sleep and waking, which runs on about a 24 hour clock. A circadian rhythm sleep disorder puts a person's sleep out of step with the demands of daily life.
the body clock is set later than normal. The person cannot fall asleep until very late, such as 3 am, and finds it hard to wake for morning school or work.
work hours fall during the usual sleep time, such as night shifts. The person struggles to sleep when they can, and feels sleepy when they need to be awake.
Both disorders can cause tiredness, poor concentration and poor functioning at school, work and in social life.
draft.remember: These disorders are a mismatch between the body clock and the hours a person must keep.

a.q: Which description best fits delayed sleep phase syndrome?
opts: Sleep cannot start until very late, so mornings are hard
Waking very early and being too sleepy by early evening
Being unable to sleep because of working night shifts
Sleeping too little because of a noisy bedroom
a.why: In delayed sleep phase syndrome the body clock is set later than normal. Night shift problems are tempting, but that describes shift work disorder, which is caused by work hours.
a.clue: Think about a body clock set later than normal.

b.q: Tomas is a nurse who works nights. On days off he cannot sleep at normal hours and feels very tired at work. Which disorder fits best, and why?
opts: Shift work disorder, as his work hours clash with his clock
Delayed sleep phase syndrome, as his body clock is set later
Shift work disorder, as he sleeps too long in the day
Delayed sleep phase syndrome, as he chooses to work late
b.why: His sleep problems come from work hours that clash with the body's usual cycle, which is shift work disorder. Delayed sleep phase syndrome is tempting because he sleeps late, but it is a body clock set later, not caused by a work roster.
b.clue: Look for what is causing the mismatch.
